'''Colin Simms''' (born 1939) is a British biologist, curator, and poet.<ref name="Guardian">{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/books/2015/aug/08/hen-harrier-poems-colin-simms-review-robert-macfarlane |title=Hen Harrier Poems by Colin Simms review – a remarkable tribute to an endangered bird |work=The Guardian |author1=Macfarlane |date=8 August 2015 |accessdate=1 October 2019|first=Rob}}</ref>

==Career==
===Biologist and curator===
Simms was appointed Keeper of Biology at the [[Yorkshire Museum]] in 1964.<ref name="North Yorkshire County Council1" details="p. 131.">{{cite book |title=The History of the Yorkshire Museum and its Geological Collections |author1=Pyrah |date=1988 |publisher=North Yorkshire County Council |page=|first=Barbara|url=https://archive.org/details/historyofyorkshi0000pyra|author-link=Barbara Pyrah}}</ref> He held this position until 1982.<ref name="North Yorkshire County Council1" details="p. 142." />

===Poet===
Simms has produced several collections, and more than forty pamphlets, of poetry, inspired by wildlife and the natural world.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.geraldengland.co.uk/revs/bs019.htm |title=COLIN SIMMS: OTTERS AND MARTENS |publisher= |author1=England |date=December 2007|website=NEW HOPE INTERNATIONAL REVIEW|first=Gerald}}</ref> These works were collected into a series of publications by Shearsman Books. The first publication was ''Otters and Martens'' in 2004, followed by ''The American Poems'' (2005), ''Gyrfalcon Poems'' (2007), ''Poems from Afghanistan'' (2013), and ''Hen Harrier Poems''.<ref name='Guardian' />

In a 2015 ''Guardian'' review of ''Hen Harrier Poems'', Simms' poetry of the last half-century was described as of "huge importance, thrilling for the rigour and commitment of its vision".<ref name='Guardian' /> He won third prize in the inaugural [[Laurel Prize (poetry)|Laurel Prize]] for environmental poetry in 2020, for ''Hen Harrier''.<ref name="laurel2020">{{Cite web |title=The Laurel Prize 2020 – Winners! |url=https://www.simonarmitage.com/the-laurel-prize-2020-winners/ |access-date=2026-10-19 |website=Simon Armitage |language=en}}</ref> He has also been described as "one of the greatest and most neglected of all Yorkshire’s poets of landscape."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2011-05-13 |title=A host of golden words that show landscape in new light |url=https://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/news/a-host-of-golden-words-that-show-landscape-in-new-light-1932715 |access-date=2026-10-19 |website=Yorkshire Post |language=en}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
*1968: "[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/209404#page/256/mode/1up A List of Botanical and Zoological Collections at the Yorkshire Museum, York], ''The Naturalist'' 904.
*1970: ''Lives of British Lizards'', Goose and Son.
*1973: ''Birches and Other Striplings'', Headland Poetry.
*1973: ''Modesty: Swaledale Summer)'', Headland Poetry.
*1974: ''Horcum and Other Gods'', Headland Poetry.
*1976: ''No Northwestern Passage: A Long-Poem'', [[Writers Forum]].
*1977: ''Parfleche'', Galloping Dog Press.
*1977: ''On Osgodby Cliffs: Poems for Cleveland'', The Curlew Press.
*1980: ''Missouri River Songs '75-'77'', Genera.
*1980: ''Movement'', Pig Press.
*1981: ''A Celebration of the Stones in a Water-course'', Galloping Dog Press.
*1987: ''Eyes Own Ideas'', Pig Press.
*2004: ''Otters and Martens'', Shearsman Books.
*2005: ''The American Poems'', Shearsman Books.
*2007: ''Gyrfalcon Poems'', Shearsman Books.
*2013: ''Poems from Afghanistan'', Shearsman Books.
*2015. ''Hen Harrier Poems'', Shearsman Books.
